compiled_state.description:
# Finish ADR 0056: extract build_agent_kwargs and the post-call telemetry from run()

## Context / Problem

`PydanticAIRunner.run()` is the last un-decomposed stretch of ADR 0056
(`docs/adr/0056-decompose-pydantic-ai-runner-run.md`). Earlier stories in epic 061c landed the
first three of the ADR's four named extractions — `interpret_failure` (e6bd),
`build_model_settings` / `build_usage_limits` (8229), and the `with ProviderSession(cfg)` guard.
The fourth, `build_agent_kwargs`, plus the post-call telemetry block the ADR's Consequences
section names by name, are still inline.

MEASURED on this branch (`src/rebar/llm/runner.py`, worktree `feat/5e75-adr0056`):

- `runner.py` was **699 LOC** when this ticket was written, one line under a `runner.py < 700`
  assertion then present in `tests/unit/test_structured_run_seam.py`. SUPERSEDED: that assertion
  has since been REMOVED under ticket db7f / ADR 0058, which makes
  `.github/module-size-limit.txt` (800) the sole authoritative ceiling. The one-line-headroom
  urgency is therefore gone; it is recorded here only as the original motivation.
- `PydanticAIRunner.run()` spans `runner.py:259-600` = **342 lines**, still 49% of the file and
  far from ADR 0056's projected 60-90.

The problem is the one-line headroom, and the people with it are every contributor who has to
touch the runner next (task cb6f and the provider-seam epic both queue lines into this cluster).

## Approach

Extract three inline blocks out of `run()` into ONE new sibling module,
`src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py`, as plain functions with explicit parameters (ADR 0056 decision 3;
no carrier object — no signature reaches the ADR's ~6-parameter threshold for one).

This is a **pure relocation**: no renamed public symbol, no changed signature crossing a module
boundary, no logic "improved" in transit, no comment losing a measured fact, a bug/story id, a
`file:line`, or a stated invariant (the constraint this ticket inherits from 7f86).

**1. `build_agent_kwargs(cfg, req, tools, toolsets, *, model_settings, web_caps) -> dict`**

Today three separated statements all write the SAME `kwargs` dict that is handed to
`Agent(model, **kwargs)` at `runner.py:481` and to `_pai_structured(...)` at `runner.py:496-498`:

- `runner.py:371-382` — the `tool_step_limit` rewrite of `tools`/`toolsets` into a filtered
  `FunctionToolset` (its only purpose is to produce the two values the dict then stores).
- `runner.py:384-392` — the base dict (`system_prompt`, `tools`, `toolsets`, `tool_timeout`).
- `runner.py:436-437` — `kwargs["capabilities"] = web_caps`.
- `runner.py:460-461` — `kwargs["model_settings"] = model_settings`.

The seam is real and already exists in the data flow: `tools`/`toolsets` are read nowhere in
`run()` after `runner.py:382` except by the dict at `384-387`, and `kwargs` is read nowhere
between its construction at `384` and its two consumers at `481`/`497`. So the four fragments
collapse into one call sited where the last of them stands today, with no statement crossing
another statement's read or write. `build_agent_kwargs` also consumes the output of
`build_model_settings` (`runner.py:441-443`), which ADR 0056 already extracted — the two are
adjacent links in one chain, which is why the ADR names them together in decision 3.

`web_caps` is passed IN rather than computed inside, deliberately: `_anthropic_web_search_capabilities`
is a `runner` module global reachable by `monkeypatch.setattr(runner_mod, ...)`, and moving its
CALL SITE into another module would silently defeat any such patch (the hazard ADR 0056's
Consequences section records). Keeping the call at `runner.py:433-435` means **zero monkeypatch
repoints are required by this change** — verified against the patch inventory below.

**2. `log_call_success(usage, *, call_label, execution_mode, ran_model, req_limit, eff_max_iter, started_at)`**

`runner.py:547-565` — the 19-line success-path `logger.info` with the step-usage counters. This
is the block ADR 0056's Consequences section names as one of the two reasons its earlier
~250/~15 projection was wrong.

It is extracted **in place**, called from `runner.py:547`, NOT folded together with the spend
record below. `_findings.finalize_outcome` at `runner.py:566-578` can raise (schema validation);
today the "ok" line is already emitted when it does. Moving the log after finalization would lose
that line on a finalization failure — a behaviour change, which a pure refactor may not make.

**3. `record_call_spend(usage, *, call_label, ran_model)`**

`runner.py:583-599` — the `usage_log.active_step()` / `usage_log.record(...)` spend row. Same
post-call telemetry concern, same `usage`/`call_label`/`ran_model` inputs as (2); it stays a
separate function only because it must stay on the far side of `finalize_outcome`. Its
`infer_provider(ran_model)` call moves with it, and `infer_provider` is then dropped from
`runner.py:38`'s import — confirmed unused elsewhere in `runner.py` and imported from `runner` by
no module or test (`grep -rn "runner import.*infer_provider" src/ tests/ docs/` is empty).

### Why a NEW module and not `structured_run.py`

The ticket's original scope line named `structured_run.py` as the destination. That is not
viable, and the evidence is in-repo: `structured_run.py` is **491 LOC** and
`tests/unit/test_structured_run_seam.py:59` asserts `100 <= loc < 500` on it (AGENTS.md's 200-500
target band). It has **9 lines of headroom** — it cannot absorb a ~130-line extraction without
either failing that assertion or forcing an edit to a structural guard another story just wrote.

`agent_call.py` is sized honestly rather than to clear a floor: the relocated source is 62 lines
of `runner.py` today (22 + 2 + 2 + 19 + 17), and signatures, contract docstrings, imports and the
module docstring bring it to roughly 130-150 — inside AGENTS.md's 200-500 target's lower half and
clear of the 100-LOC anti-fragmentation floor with real content, not padding.

Its cohesion is stated plainly rather than overclaimed: the three functions do **not** call each
other. What binds them is that they are the edges of exactly one Agent call — the kwargs handed
to `Agent(...)`, and the two records emitted after it returns — and they share `run()`'s locals
(`usage`, `ran_model`, `call_label`, `req_limit`, `eff_max_iter`). `structured_run.py` keeps its
own distinct job (driving the structured-output retry loop and computing settings) and is not
edited at all by this change.

`agent_call.py` is a LEAF on the same rule as `structured_run.py`: it imports nothing from
`runner` at runtime; the one `RunRequest` annotation is deferred via
`from __future__ import annotations` + `TYPE_CHECKING`, so `import rebar.llm` stays stdlib-only.

### Monkeypatch-hazard audit (the constraint 7f86 flagged as LIVE)

The full inventory of `monkeypatch.setattr(runner_mod, ...)` targets in the suite is
`_import_pydantic_ai`, `capabilities_for`, `ProviderSession`, `build_usage_limits`,
`_pai_structured`, `_pai_model`, `cache_settings_for`, `_local_proxy_bypass_base_url`, and
`get_runner`. **Every one of them stays a `runner` module global under this plan** — none is
called from inside a relocated block, and `_anthropic_web_search_capabilities` is kept at its
current call site precisely to preserve that. So this change requires **zero** repoints, and the
ADR's "each repoint lands in the same commit" rule is satisfied vacuously.

`tests/unit/test_llm_timeouts.py:332-334` asserts `"signal.alarm" not in inspect.getsource(runner_mod)`
and `"Timer(" not in ...`; removing lines only narrows that negative-space guard, so it stays green.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — remove the four `kwargs` fragments and the two telemetry blocks;
  add the three calls and one import; drop the now-unused `infer_provider` import.
- `src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py` — NEW; the three extracted functions.
- `tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py` — NEW; the structural seam test, following the convention
  of `tests/unit/test_structured_run_seam.py` and `tests/unit/test_interpret_failure_seam.py`.

No other file changes. `src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py` is NOT edited.

## Testing

A relocation adds no behaviour, so the real regression net is the **existing suite passing
unedited** — no assertion weakened, skipped, deleted, or adjusted. The baseline pass count is
recorded before the first edit and must match after.

The new seam test asserts the structure the move has to preserve, and covers a failure/edge path
rather than the happy path only:

- Happy path: `build_agent_kwargs` with `tool_step_limit=None` returns `tools`/`toolsets`
  unchanged and `tool_timeout == float(cfg.llm_tool_timeout_s)`; worked example — with
  `cfg.llm_tool_timeout_s = 77` and `tools=[t]`, the result is
  `{"system_prompt": ..., "tools": [t], "toolsets": [], "tool_timeout": 77.0}`.
- Edge: with `tool_step_limit=3` and a non-empty `tools`, the result has `tools == []` and every
  entry of `toolsets` filtered — the convergence-boundary rewrite, whose absence would silently
  un-bound a tool loop.
- Edge: `model_settings=None`/falsy and `web_caps=None` omit the `"model_settings"` and
  `"capabilities"` keys entirely (the "byte-identical for a non-anthropic request" invariant at
  `runner.py:430-432`).
- Edge: `log_call_success` on an empty `usage` dict emits its line with zeroed counters and does
  not raise (`usage` is `{}` whenever the call failed before usage extraction).
- Structural: `agent_call.py >= 100` (the anti-fragmentation floor; NO upper ceiling on
  `runner.py` — see ADR 0058), and `agent_call.py` has no
  runtime import of `runner` (AST-checked, same method as
  `test_structured_run_seam.py::test_structured_run_has_no_runtime_import_from_runner`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `build_agent_kwargs` exists in `src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py` as a plain function with
      explicit parameters and no carrier object, and `runner.py` builds the Agent kwargs by
      calling it — verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py` and by
      `grep -c 'kwargs: dict\[str, Any\] = {' src/rebar/llm/runner.py` returning 0.
- [ ] The success-path `logger.info` telemetry block and the `usage_log.record` spend block are
      both out of `run()` and in `agent_call.py` as `log_call_success` / `record_call_spend` —
      verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py`.
- [ ] `tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py` asserts that `agent_call.py` clears the 100-LOC
      anti-fragmentation floor — verified by that test passing. It must NOT assert any upper LOC
      ceiling on `runner.py`: ADR 0058 makes `.github/module-size-limit.txt` (800) the SOLE
      authoritative ceiling, enforced by the CI module-size gate and mirrored in-process by
      `tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py`, which reads that same file. Per-file ceilings
      asserted in seam tests were removed under ticket db7f as overreach — they invert governance
      (the tightest bound becomes an unlocked literal) and fail mid-refactor by construction.
      Narrowed from the original "under 700 LOC AND ..." wording after ADR 0058 landed; the
      floor half is retained because it is the opposite check and catches what the cap cannot.
- [ ] The full default selection
      (`pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 6 --dist worksteal -q`) passes with a pass
      count at least the pre-change baseline and zero failures, with **no existing test edited** —
      verified by diffing the recorded baseline count against the post-change count and by
      `git diff --stat` showing no modified file under `tests/` (only the new seam test added).
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` both exit 0.
- [ ] No relocated comment lost a measured number, a `file:line`, a bug/story/epic id, a named
      failure mode, or a stated invariant — verified by `git show --stat` plus reading the moved
      comment blocks against their originals in the diff.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The before/after LOC for `runner.py` AND for the `PydanticAIRunner.run()`
      METHOD BODY are recorded in the commit message. Tagged because the completion verifier reads
      repository files only and cannot read git history; the method figure is tracked separately
      because it is the number ADR 0056 has twice under-projected (260, then 310, MEASURED 323
      after 7f86, 342 today). Evidence recorded on the ticket: a comment quoting both figures and
      the commit SHA that carries them.
- [ ] [operator-attested] Zero monkeypatch repoints were required, and the commit message says so
      with the reason (no relocated block calls a patched `runner` global). Evidence recorded on
      the ticket: a comment naming the audited target list and the commit SHA.
